intersection_proof.reason: f_dice SHA256 input: variable-length ASCII {0x31..0x36}^n; f_yas SHA256 input: fixed 32-byte full-range binary. Structurally incompatible, collision probability < 2^{-128}

math_proof_dice.theorem: When user rolls dice only N times, the effective entropy of mnemonic set M_N is H = N·log2(6) ≈ 2.585N bit
proof: 1. import_from_dice(rolls) accepts rolls ∈ {1..6}^N, no minimum length restriction
2. entropy = SHA256(b'' + ascii(rolls)), where ascii('1')=0x31..ascii('6')=0x36
3. SHA256 as collision-resistant hash, different inputs produce different outputs (probability 1 - 2^{-128})
4. Input space |{1..6}^N| = 6^N, therefore |M_N| = 6^N
5. H_eff(N) = log2(6^N) = N·log2(6) ≈ 2.585N bit
6. N=1: H=2.585bit; N=10: H=25.85bit; N=50: H=129.25bit (security threshold)
math_proof_dice.qed: When N<50, H < 128 bit, does not meet BIP-39 security requirement; device should enforce N≥50

math_proof_yasmarang.theorem: When Mk3 firmware erroneously links yasmarang, mnemonic set |M| ≤ 2^32
proof: 1. MICROPY_HW_ENABLE_RNG=0 causes rng_get() to link MicroPython yasmarang PRNG
2. yasmarang internal state: (pad, n, d) initialized to (pad_init, 0, 0)
3. pad_init ∈ [0, 2^32), the only free parameter
4. make_new_wallet() calls my_random_bytes(32) → 8 rng_get() calls
5. MicroPython yasmarang output 32 bit × 8 = 256 bit, entirely determined by pad_init
6. libngu yasmarang output is also deterministic (no true random seed internally)
7. final_entropy = XOR(mpy_yas_output, libngu_yas_output), both deterministic
8. mnemonic = BIP39(SHA256(final_entropy)), deterministic function chain
9. |M| ≤ |{pad_init}| = 2^32, H_eff ≤ 32 bit
math_proof_yasmarang.qed: Affected Mk3 device mnemonics can be recovered within 2^32 brute-force attempts (~7min @10M/s)

mathpoc.key_insight: Pure function, no RNG, input entirely determined by user dice characters

math_proof.theorem: In browsers without WebCrypto, the private key set K generated by bitaddress.org has cardinality |K| ≤ 2^31
proof: 1. Let IE JScript Math.random() internal state be s ∈ [0, 2^31), LCG: s' = (214013·s + 2531011) mod 2^31
2. SecureRandom pool initialization calls Math.random() 128 times, each taking floor(65536·output)
3. Since LCG is a deterministic function, 128 outputs are entirely determined by initial state s_0: pool = g(s_0)
4. ARC4.init(pool) is a deterministic function of pool: arc4_state = h(pool) = h(g(s_0))
5. privkey = (ARC4.next()^32 mod (n-1)) + 1, a deterministic function of arc4_state
6. Therefore privkey = f(s_0), the entire mapping f: [0, 2^31) → secp256k1 is deterministic
8. Effective entropy H_eff = log2(|K|) ≤ 31 bit ≪ 128 bit (BIP security threshold)
math_proof.qed: Any private key generated by bitaddress.org without WebCrypto can be brute-forced within 2^31 attempts

math_proof.theorem: Trust Wallet WASM extension (v0.0.172-v0.0.182) mnemonic set M has cardinality |M| ≤ 2^32
proof: 1. random_buffer(buf, 16) creates mt19937 rng(std::random_device{}())
2. std::random_device{}() returns uint32_t seed ∈ [0, 2^32)
3. mt19937 initialization: MT[0] = seed; MT[i] = f(MT[i-1], i) for i=1..623
4. The entire 624×32-bit internal state is uniquely determined by a single 32-bit seed
5. generate_n(buf, 16, [&rng]{ return rng() & 0xFF; }) takes low 8 bits of first 16 twist outputs
6. entropy[16] = g(seed), where g: uint32 → byte[16] is a deterministic function
7. mnemonic = BIP39(entropy) is a deterministic mapping
8. Therefore mnemonic = BIP39(g(seed)), complete mapping h: [0, 2^32) → Mnemonic_12word
10. Effective entropy H_eff = log2(|M|) ≤ 32 bit ≪ 128 bit (BIP-39 standard)
math_proof.qed: Any 12-word mnemonic generated by affected versions can be brute-forced within 2^32 attempts

math_proof.theorem: 128-bit entropy generated by CryptoJS 3.x WordArray.random(16) has effective search space |S| ≤ 2^40
proof: 1. WordArray.random(16) generates 4 32-bit words, loops 4 times
2. First round: m_w_init = Math.random() * 0x100000000, effective 32 bits
3. Each round creates MWC(m_w_init), called 2 times: 1st computes rcache, 2nd computes output word
4. Each call appends Math.random() > 0.5 check, introducing 1 bit sign
5. Subsequent rounds: m_w_init deterministically derived from rcache, no new independent entropy
6. Total independent parameters: 1 seed (32 bit) + 8 sign bits (4 rounds × 2 calls) = 40 bit
7. Some sign combinations produce collisions (sign ineffective when MWC output=0), actual |S| ≈ 2^39
8. H_eff ≈ 39-40 bit ≪ 128 bit (BIP-39 security threshold)
math_proof.qed: Any 12-word BIP39 mnemonic generated by CryptoJS 3.x can be brute-forced within ~2^39 attempts

math_proof.theorem: Private keys generated by getrandbits(256) after random.seed(int(time.time())) have effective search space |K| ≤ T_window
proof: 1. random.seed(t) calls init_by_array for integer t, initializing MT19937's 624×32-bit internal state
2. Initialization is a deterministic function: same t → same internal state → same output sequence
3. random.getrandbits(256) takes first 8 MT19937 32-bit outputs combined into 256-bit integer
4. Therefore privkey = f(t), where f: int → [0, 2^256) is a deterministic mapping
5. If t = int(time.time()), then t ∈ [T_start, T_end), T_window = T_end - T_start
6. Time window 2009-01-03 to 2015-12-31: T_window = 220,599,895 seconds
8. H_eff = log2(|K|) ≈ 27.7 bit ≪ 128 bit
math_proof.qed: Any private key generated by random.seed(timestamp) can be brute-forced in ~20 minutes (@180K/s Python)

mathpoc.key_insight: Python random is a deterministic PRNG; seed(time.time()) compresses search space to time window in seconds

math_proof.theorem: All mnemonics generated by libbitcoin bx seed have set size |M| ≤ 2^32
proof: 1. bx seed calls pseudo_random::fill(), internally uses thread_local std::mt19937
2. MT19937 seed = static_cast<uint32_t>(high_resolution_clock::now().time_since_epoch().count())
3. uint32_t truncation: seed ∈ [0, 2^32), only 32 bits
4. std::mt19937 is deterministic PRNG: seed → completely determined output sequence
5. bx seed 128 takes low 8 bits of MT output × 16 = 16 bytes entropy
6. entropy → BIP39 mnemonic is a deterministic mapping
7. Therefore mnemonic = f(seed), f: [0, 2^32) → Mnemonic_12word
math_proof.qed: Any 12-word mnemonic generated by bx seed 128 can be brute-forced within 2^32 attempts
